In the rollout-temperature ablation (Figure 5), the **naive Parallel-RL model reaches about 84.6% on MATH500 at τ = 0.8**, and the **math model reaches about 87.2% at τ = 0.75** (p. 23).

These are estimates from the plot. The figure has no data labels and the text gives no exact values, so the readings could be off by roughly ±0.1–0.2 points.

- **Naive Parallel-RL at τ = 0.8:** This is the last point on its curve. It is lower than the curve's peak of about 86.0% near τ ≈ 0.65, which the paper calls the "sweet spot" (p. 23).
- **Math model at τ = 0.75:** This is the highest point on its curve, with a slight drop to about 87.0% at τ = 0.8 (p. 23).

The paper says the math model's accuracy improves as τ rises from 0.4 to 0.8. Meanwhile, the Parallel-RL accuracy "first increases and then degrades" because more exploration increases variance within each group of rollouts, which in turn increases interference between tasks (p. 23). The ablation used LoRA on a subset of the data because of resource constraints (p. 23).
